I just finished World War Z, and I thought there were several topics and themes that were interesting and worthy of discussion. I'll list a few here, feel free to bring up any other you like.

  • How does people respond to global scares, such as epidemics or catastrophe warnings? Would anyone take an actual outbreak seriously, or would it play out just like Brooks describes?
  • Is government the only means of salvation in a situation like this? Is a centralised authority a requirement for global organisation?
  • Would humans be as much of a threat to each other as the zombies (or equivalent) are? Would there be chaos or solidarity?

Over all an interesting and entertaining read, and put in real life context, actually quite scary.

In a realistic scenario the disease that turns people into zombies might be devestating, depending on how it's transmitted, but the actual zombies themselves would pose very little real threat. The idea of zombies overrunning any modern military force is laughable; a single tank could take out a near infinite amount of zombies. Even without tanks, the killing power of just a few people with grenade launchers and machine guns would be more than enough to take out very large zombie hordes.

That's what you'd think... but unless you destroy the brain (or remove their arms and legs), the zombies will just keep coming.

And even if you do remove the extremities, destroying the brain is the only way to make sure the zombie is no longer a threat... which is part of the reason why the Battle of Yonkers in World War Z was such a spectacular failure.

Seriously, read the book sometime, particularly the section that deals with the Battle of Yonkers.

I actually have read the book; I really enjoyed it, but not all parts of it were realistic. The description of the Battle of the Yonkers was one of the most unrealistic parts of the book; there is absolutely no way a horde of zombies could take down a tank. All the tank has to do is drive back and forth, running over zombies in the process.

This is just a general problem with Zombies is that zombies are really only ever successful because in the world where a zombie apocalypse happens, there isn't a bunch of speculative fiction detailing how exactly they work and allowing people a bunch of time to prepare optimal plans for surviving in the situation.
